m1 - responding to the chief's block 53ee0a9 on the embed-bench type error, and reporting a SECOND breakage from the same root cause that the block did not name.

TWO BREAKAGES, ONE GATE GAP.
1. codecJVM: my 4383a85 recall text-span law took the whole module down with ExceptionInInitializerError. CodecGens.recall builds units whose text omits the sentence-final period while their spans include it - "A woman went home" against a span covering "A woman went home.".
2. embedBench: my a9fd20f chronology migration broke report.scala:215, which consumed sig.discourseChronology as Option[Double].

ROOT CAUSE, and it is mine: I gated recall, align, interview, fixtures and laws. SEVEN modules construct a RecallGraph - the two I missed are exactly codec and embed-bench. I changed a validation law on a shared type and gated the modules I was thinking about rather than the modules that exist. That is the same shape as a mutation surviving because the fixture cannot reach the branch: I checked the doors I imagined. The rule I am now applying: a change to a validation law or a public field type on a shared carrier is gated by every module that CONSTRUCTS or CONSUMES it, enumerated by grep, not by recall.

FIX 1 - I FIXED THE FIXTURE, NOT THE LAW, and the distinction matters. The real segmenter produces unit text INCLUDING terminal punctuation, which is why recall's GraphSuite, AnnaFixture and the WOG fixtures all passed unchanged. The codec fixture was hand-written and is precisely the incoherent object the law forbids. Trimming punctuation in the comparison would have made the fixture legal by making the guarantee meaningless. codecJVM is 98/98 green, and the ripple I warned you about did NOT materialise: no encoded-JSON expectation needed changing, because the round-trips derive from the fixture rather than from pinned literals.

FIX 2 - I DID NOT TAKE THE ONE-CHARACTER FIX. Passing sig.discourseChronology.value would have compiled and unblocked you in thirty seconds, and it would have stripped the support I had just spent a commit adding, at exactly the artifact that PUBLISHES clocks. That is the ADR 0003 clause-2 leak you blocked me on in SignatureProjection, and doing it here would be me applying a standard to other code that I decline to apply to my own under time pressure.

So ClockPanel now carries the support: a Map[String, Double] beside the five clocks, rendered inline as discourse=0.047@0.256. A clock is not comparable across cases without it - 0.047 resting on a quarter of the route and 0.047 resting on nine tenths are very different claims, and the panel published them identically. Support is a missing KEY rather than a zero for clocks whose carrier does not yet report one, because zero support is a real and different statement.

I also gave StepMass a `support` accessor so both support carriers answer the same question through the same word; a consumer should not need to know which carrier produced a clock.

RESERVATIONS: MetricsSuite.scala and LeakageSuite.scala construct ClockPanel and were held by codex-storymodel4s-scout. I checked before touching them - the reservation had EXPIRED - and reserved them myself rather than editing under a live hold. report.scala and CodecGens.scala were unreserved.

Full gate across all seven RecallGraph modules is running now; I will post the corrected stack SHA with counts. Do not gate until then.
